milestones.title: Hyderabad founded
milestones.detail: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, fifth Qutb Shahi king of Golconda, laid out a new city on the south bank of the Musi, with the Charminar at the crossing of its four main roads.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India (1908), vol. 13, 'Hyderabad City', pp. 308-311, https://archive.org/details/imperialgazettee13grea

milestones.title: Mughal conquest
milestones.detail: Aurangzeb's army stormed Golconda and Hyderabad passed to the Mughal Empire.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India (1908), vol. 13, 'Hyderabad City', pp. 308-311, https://archive.org/details/imperialgazettee13grea

milestones.title: Asaf Jah I establishes the Nizams' rule
milestones.detail: Asaf Jah I defeated the Mughal governor Mubariz Khan and founded the Asaf Jahi dynasty. The stone city wall begun by Mubariz Khan was completed under the first Nizam.
milestones.source: Richards, The Mughal Empire, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyderabad; city wall: Imperial Gazetteer of India (1908), vol. 13, 'Hyderabad City', pp. 308-311, https://archive.org/details/imperialgazettee13grea

milestones.title: Capital of the Nizams
milestones.detail: Hyderabad city became the formal capital of the Asaf Jahi Nizams.
milestones.source: Richards, The Mughal Empire; Ikram, Muslim Civilization in India, http://www.columbia.edu/itc/mealac/pritchett/00islamlinks/ikram/part2_19.html, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyderabad

milestones.title: Secunderabad cantonment founded
milestones.detail: The Nizam allotted land north of Hussain Sagar for a British cantonment, the origin of Hyderabad's twin city Secunderabad.

milestones.title: Railway reaches the city
milestones.detail: The Nizam's Guaranteed State Railway opened from Secunderabad to Wadi, linking Hyderabad to the Great Indian Peninsula Railway.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India (1908), vol. 13, 'Hyderabad State', https://archive.org/details/imperialgazettee13grea

milestones.title: Great Musi flood
milestones.detail: On 27-28 September 1908 the Musi rose about 12 ft above its bridges and swept them away. A large, densely populated part of the city was wrecked and thousands of people died.

milestones.title: Osman Sagar dam completed
milestones.detail: A dam was built across the Musi about ten miles upstream of the city to prevent a repeat of the 1908 flood; the reservoir also became a main source of drinking water.

milestones.title: Hyderabad State annexed by India
milestones.detail: On 17 September 1948 the Indian Army took control of Hyderabad State in Operation Polo, ending the Nizam's rule.

milestones.title: Capital of Andhra Pradesh
milestones.detail: On 1 November 1956 the states were reorganised by language and Hyderabad became the capital of the new state of Andhra Pradesh.

milestones.title: HITEC City inaugurated
milestones.detail: The Cyber Towers technology park was inaugurated on 22 November 1998, starting the growth of the western IT district.

milestones.title: Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation formed
milestones.detail: The municipal area grew from 175 km2 to 650 km2 when surrounding municipalities were merged into the new corporation.
milestones.source: Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation, Corporation History, https://www.ghmc.gov.in/CorporationHistory.aspx, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyderabad

milestones.title: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport opens
milestones.detail: The new airport at Shamshabad, about 24 km south of the city, opened on 23 March 2008 and replaced Begumpet Airport.

milestones.title: Capital of the new state of Telangana
milestones.detail: Telangana was formed on 2 June 2014 with Hyderabad as its capital; the city also remained the common capital of Andhra Pradesh for up to ten years.
milestones.source: Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyderabad

milestones.title: Hyderabad Metro opens
milestones.detail: A 30 km stretch from Miyapur to Nagole with 24 stations was inaugurated on 28 November 2017.

landmarks.name: Purana Pul
landmarks.source: Height (54 ft above the river bed): Imperial Gazetteer of India (1908), vol. 13, 'Hyderabad City', pp. 308-311, https://archive.org/details/imperialgazettee13grea; date: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purana_pul
landmarks.note: Built under the Golconda sultans before the city itself. Wikipedia dates it to 1578; the 1908 Imperial Gazetteer says 1593.

landmarks.name: Charminar
landmarks.note: Minarets rise 48.7 m above ground. The 1908 Imperial Gazetteer gives 180 ft (54.9 m) and some sources quote 56 m.

landmarks.name: Mecca Masjid
landmarks.source: Height (75 ft): Imperial Gazetteer of India (1908), vol. 13, 'Hyderabad City', pp. 308-311, https://archive.org/details/imperialgazettee13grea; completion: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makkah_Masjid,_Hyderabad
landmarks.note: Begun in 1617 and completed under Aurangzeb in 1694. Height is that of the main hall as given in the Gazetteer.

landmarks.name: Buddha Statue of Hyderabad
landmarks.note: 58 ft monolith installed on its platform in Hussain Sagar on 1 December 1992; height excludes the platform.

landmarks.name: Lodha Bellezza 3
landmarks.note: Hyderabad's first 150 m+ building according to CTBUH.

landmarks.name: Statue of Equality
landmarks.note: 216 ft as reported at its inauguration on 5 February 2022; at Muchintal, about 25 km from the old city.

landmarks.name: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Telangana State Secretariat
landmarks.note: 265 ft to the national emblem on the central dome; inaugurated 30 April 2023.

landmarks.name: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Statue
landmarks.note: 125 ft statue unveiled 14 April 2023. Height excludes the plinth, which Wikipedia gives as a further 50 ft.

landmarks.name: My Home Nishada Tower 1
landmarks.note: Tallest completed building in Hyderabad according to CTBUH (one of eight equal towers).

landmarks.name: SAS Crown Tower 1
landmarks.note: CTBUH status when checked (November 2026): architecturally topped out, expected completion 2026. One of three equal towers.

notes: Start date: the standard date for the founding is 1591 (AH 1000), the year the Charminar was built; older references such as the 1908 Imperial Gazetteer and the 1911 Britannica give 1589 for the founding. A legend links the city's first name, Bhagnagar, to Bhagmati. Golconda fort, five miles west, is older and was the capital before the city was laid out. Population: figures before 1881 are Chandler's estimates and are rough; his 70,000 for the founding year is high for a newly laid-out city and should be read with caution (he lists Golconda separately at 45,000 in 1585). 1881 and 1891 are census counts as reported in the Imperial Gazetteer (city with suburbs, Residency Bazars and cantonment). 1901-1941 are the Census of India's back-cast series for the Hyderabad urban agglomeration, which includes Secunderabad. The census series falls between 1911 and 1921; the cause was not researched here. Landmarks left out for lack of a sourced structural height: Golconda Fort, the Qutb Shahi tombs, Chowmahalla and Falaknuma palaces, the High Court, Osmania University Arts College, Cyber Towers and the Durgam Cheruvu cable bridge. The Charminar's height is given differently by different sources (48.7 m, 54.9 m, 56 m); the tourism ministry's 48.7 m is used. Purana Pul's date is disputed (1578 or 1593). CTBUH lists several taller towers under construction (to 243 m) that are not included.
